newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end stronger, focus moves to payrolls.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end stronger, focus moves to payrolls.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed much stronger on Wednesday, matching gains in U.S. Treasuries during the past two sessions, with investors now focusing on tomorrow's U.S. payrolls data for June, analysts said.

"Now we're back on I would say an even footing with the U.S. market and both markets are waiting to see the non-farm payrolls number tomorrow," said Rod Kerr, a bond portfolio manager with Laketon Investment Management. "(The Fed decision) didn't have much of an impact."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$1.42 to C$115.37 from Monday's close to yield 6.791 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 11/32 to yield 6.72 percent. The spread between the bonds was seven basis points, unchanged from the close of trading on Monday.

Canadian bonds stopped trading at noon on Monday ahead of Tuesday's Canada Day public and market holiday, when U.S. Treasuries recorded strong gains. The Canadian bond quickly matched those gains when today's trading session began.

The Canadian market took direction from U.S. Treasuries for the remainder of today's session, with the decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee to hold rates steady having little impact on either market.
"It was not a surprise and you've still got that non-farm payroll number staring you in the face," said Lee.

The U.S. non-farm payrolls report for June will be released tomorrow at 830 EDT/1230 GMT. The report is seen as a key indication of the economy's strength and is expected to give clues about the timing of the next U.S. rate hike.

In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.88 to C$107.45 from Monday's close to yield 6.223 percent, compared to its U.S. equivalent which rose 6/32 this session to yield 6.42 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds was 20 basis points, unchanged from the close of trading on Monday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.14 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.23 percent.
